Complainant : State by, Police Sub Inspector  J.B.Nagar, Police Station  V/s.
 Accused : Akshay A.S  S/o. A/C/Subramanya,
 Aged about 30 years,
 R/at. No. P-240, 9th Main,
 LIC Colony, J.B.Nagar,
 Bengaluru.
JUDGMENT

The PSI of J.B. Nagar police station has filed this chargesheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/s. 341, 323, 504, 498(A) of IPC.
2.
It is the case of the prosecution that, CW1 got married to accused on 15/11/2004 as per the customs of Kodava community.
After the marriage, CW1 was staying with her husband i.e., accused along with his mother, step-father, and brother-in-law in J.B. Nagar.
Thereafter, accused and CW1 stayed separately for two months.
During this time and when they moved back to accused's mother's house, CW1 suspected that there was some relation between accused and his marketing executive.
When CW1 questioned the accused, he picked up a fight with her and assaulted her.
He abused her in filthy language and asked her to give the child and take divorce from him and tortured her physically and mentally.
On 23/01/2011 at about 6.00 pm accused picked up a fight with CW1 and wrongfully restrained her from moving ahead, assaulted her with hands and suspected her character.
She was asked to hand over the child and take divorce from him.
He also told her that Jeevan Bheema Nagar Police Station vs Akshay.

1 there were others who were ready to give dowry and get married to him and thereby physically and mentally tortured her.
Hence, it is alleged that accused has committed the alleged offences.

3. On the basis of the FIS lodged by the informant, case was registered against the accused in J.B.
Nagar P.S., Cr. No.405/2011 and FIR was submitted to the court.
On completion of investigation charge-sheet has been filed against the accused for the alleged offences.
4. Cognizance of offence was taken and summons was issued to the accused.
Accused has appeared before the court through his counsel and he was released on bail.
Copies of charge sheet were furnished to accused U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.
After hearing, charge was framed against the accused for the alleged offences.
The accused has pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5. The prosecution in support of its case has examined seven witnesses as PW.1 & PW.2 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P1 to P14.
The statement of accused U/s.313 of Cr.P.C was recorded.
Accused did not lead any evidence.

6. Heard the arguments of Sr. APP appearing for the state and the counsel for accused and perused the records.
7.The following points arise for determination:
1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond doubt that, accused being the husband of CW1 subsequent to the marriage with CW1 on 15/11/2004 subjected her to physical and mental cruelty making it improbable for her to lead a proper marital life and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s. 498(A) of IPC ?
2) Whether the prosecution proves beyond doubt that, accused on 23/01/2011 at around 6.00 pm, at No. P-240, 9th Main, LIC colony, J.B. Nagar, Bengaluru wrongfully restrained CW1 and assaulted her with hands causing simple hurt to her and without there being any provocation abused her in filthy language and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s. 341, 323, 504 of IPC?
3) What order?
8.

2 10. CW1 Devammaji was examined as PW2, she deposed that, she got engaged to accused at Hotel Ramanashree in Bengaluru on 19/08/2004.
At the time of engagement, her parents gave one gold chain, one ring, and one silver ornament.
The accused gave her one silk saree, one fancy saree, one necklace with a ear stud and one diamond ring, as a gift.
The engagement expenses were borne by her parents.
On 15/11/2004 her marriage took place at Kodava Samaja, Vasanth Nagar, Bengaluru and her parents gave Rs. 5,00,000/- cash and gold articles weighing 100 grams to the accused.
After the marriage as per the custom she handed over the same to her mother- in-law.
Similarly she gave gold box to her mother-in-law containing 100 grams of gold coins and gold ornaments and her mother in law took half of it and returned to her.
When CW.1 asked her mother-in- law to return the gold coins, she told that she had pledged the same and refused to return the gold coins.
11. PW.2 further deposed that, within 8 days of marriage accused picked up a fight with her.
He had given false information about his education and age.
Her mother-in-law advised the CW1 and accused to make a separate house and reside in a rented house.
Accordingly, they started to reside in a rented house at J.B.Nagar.
Thereafter, due to fights between them, they returned back to her mother-in-law's house.
In her mother-in-law's house, accused assaulted her every night by consuming alcohol.
Accused used to attend late night parties regularly.

If she were to question him,
he would say that it is none of her business.
In the year 2007, when she conceived, accused got it aborted.
On 04/09/2008, the accused had a fight with his father.
When she asked the accused regarding this, he assaulted her on her left ear, due to which she had to take treatment at ENT specialist.
When she got pregnant again, accused forced her get aborted the baby.
On 06/06/2009 she gave birth to a baby boy and all the expenses were borne by her parents.
After returning to her matrimonial home, they led a happy life together for three months.
However, all of a sudden, he stopped coming home at night.
12. PW2 further deposed that on 27/07/2010, CW1, her kid and accused went to Singapore.
At that time, when she checked accused's mobile, she found pictures of a lady by name Charumathi.
After returning to Bengaluru, when CW1 called that lady Charumathi and enquired, she replied that, they are in a relationship and that they had got married.
CW1 never asked accused regarding this.
However, the lady informed accused about it and he came and fought with her.
Thereafter, accused fought with her everyday.
PW1 saw that the lady had sent an email to the accused stating that, she is ready to hide the relationship from her husband.
In the year 2011 accused and Charumathi went to Dubai for New Year's party.
Whenever she would question, accused used to ask her to get lost or else he would kill her.
In 2011 when the accused was going to Malaysia, he asked her to leave the house and asked her not to be at home when he returns.
Therefore, on 23/01/2001 she left the house of the accused.
Thereafter he issued divorce notice and she filed domestic violence case against him.
13. PW1 got marked six documents as Ex.P9 to 14.

Ex.P9 is the three certified copies of photographs,
Ex.P10 is the copy of the hotel bill, Ex.P11 is the copy of the payment receipt, Ex.P12 is the copy of NCR, Ex.P13 and 14 are the Bank Statements.
14. In her cross examination, PW2 deposed that she is staying with her son in Kammanahalli.
After she left the accused, she took her son and went to Coorg and from 2011 to 2012, she was in Coorg.
During her stay at her in-law's place, there was no problem for food and clothing but she was Jeevan Bheema Nagar Police Station vs Akshay.

3 mentally tortured.
In this regard, no complaint was lodged.
She admitted that her mother-in-law came looking for her to Coorg, but she sent her back.
CW2 and 3 are her parents and CW4 is her brother.
After 2011, she never returned to her matrimonial home
Photo album of the son is marked as Ex.D1 which contained photos taken at Innovative Film City, in front of the house of the accused and at a wedding in Hyderabad.
In 2010, she was on good terms with the accused's family but not him.
The last photo may have been taken in Mysore.
Before leaving the house in 2011, she informed her mother-in-law.
During her stay with the accused, she never visited his office.
She also admitted that, as accused paid all the expenses, the Ex.P10 bill was in his name.
She denied all the other suggestions pur forth to her.
15. CW5, Investigating officer was examined as PW1.
He deposed about having received the private complaint from the Court and registered the case and conducted the entire investigation and filed the charge-sheet.
He got marked eight documents as Ex.P1 to 8.

Ex.P1 is the Private complaint,
Ex.P2 is the FIR, Ex.P3 to 6 are the photographs, Ex.P7 is the marriage invitation card and Ex.P8 is the marriage certificate.
16. Nothing worth was elicited in his cross examination.

17. On perusal of the oral and documentary evidence, it is the allegation of the prosecution that accused subjected PW2 to physical and mental cruelty when PW2 questioned him about his affair with a colleague and thereafter, assaulted her, abused her in foul language and wrongfully restrained her.
In this case, the prosecution cited five witnesses including CW1/PW2 victim.
CW2 to 4 are the family members of PW2 who have not come forward to narrate about the alleged incident.

Hence,
the entire case is dependent on the evidence of PW2.
18. At the outset, in the evidence of PW2, she has not narrated that the accused wrongfully restrained her or abused her in foul language.
Neither the private complaint nor the oral evidence mentions the abusive words allegedly used by the accused on PW2.
Without mentioning the exact words, it cannot be held that the accused intentionally insulted PW2 to provoke her.
19. Further it is alleged that the accused had an affair with his colleague and in this regard, when she questioned the accused, he assaulted her and continued to assault her.

As per the evidence of PW2,
she last came in contact with the accused before he left for Malaysia and when he was in Malaysia,
she left the matrimonial house.
There is no document to show that accused assaulted PW2.
There are no hearsay witnesses also to speak about the same.

The oral evidence of PW2 alone is not sufficient to hold that the accused assaulted PW2.
20.
It is also alleged that accused mentally tortured her by being in a relationship with a female colleague of his.
It is elicited that accused runs his own business of tours and travels.
Ex .P9 photographs alone does not show that accused was/is in a relationship with the woman in the photograph.
Further, PW2 admits that accused paid all the bills and as such, they were in his name.
Ex . P10
bills also reflect the name of Ms. Sridevi.

Ex.P13 Bank statement shows that, on 26.11.2011,
accused transferred Rs.3,00,000/- to Charumothi.
There is no cogent proof of illicit relationship.
Hence, the said documents do no prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused was having illicit Jeevan Bheema Nagar Police Station vs Akshay.

4 relationship with Ms. Sridevi or Ms. Charumothi.

Hence the ingredients of cruelty is not met to attract the offence u/s 498A of IPC.
21.
Therefore, the cumulative effect of the entire evidence placed before the Court is that there is no cogent evidence to bring forth the guilt of the accused.
If two views are possible in a given circumstance, the one which is favourable to the accused is to be considered.
If there arises any doubt, the benefit of the same should go to the accused.
The facts and circumstances revealing from the evidence by itself are sufficient to extend benefit of doubt to the accused.
Therefore, from the entire appraisal of the evidence placed before the Court, prosecution has failed to prove the allegations against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Points No.1 and 2 in the Negative.
22. POINT NO.3:

For the aforesaid reasons, the following order is passed;
 ORDER  Acting Sec.248(1) of Cr.P.C the accused is acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 341, 323, 504, 498A of IPC.
Bail bond and surety of the accused stands canceled.
